name: aften
desc: Audio encoder which generates ATSC A/52 compressed audio streams
why: An open ATSC A/52 AC-3 audio encoder, a rare look inside a broadcast codec that most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: Aften is a command-line audio encoder that produces compressed audio streams in the ATSC A/52 format, also known as AC-3 or Dolby Digital. The homepage describes it as an encoder that generates these streams from the A/52 specification, and it is used in DVD-Video content. The homepage does not spell out the input format. The installed tools (wavfilter, wavinfo, wavrms) suggest WAV audio is the working material, but that is an inference from the executable names. The Homebrew package installs four executables: aften, wavfilter, wavinfo and wavrms.
brief.why_it_exists: The project began as a stand-alone command-line version of the FFmpeg AC-3 encoder and has since grown with structural changes and extra features. The name is an acronym for 'A Fifty-Two ENcoder', and it is also the Danish and Norwegian word for 'evening'.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage names the reference specification for the encoding algorithm and bitstream format as ATSC Standard A/52 (Revision A). It says Revision B adds E-AC-3 (Dolby Digital Plus), which the project lists as a future goal. The homepage does not describe the internal encoder pipeline.

commands_seen.context: Clones the current development source from the project's SourceForge git repository. The homepage gives this as the way to get the latest git version.

brief.install_notes: The homepage links a 'Building Aften with CMake' document, which suggests a CMake build from source, but I did not follow that link, so I have no build steps. The homepage also links 'Commandline help', which I did not follow either. Building from the git clone is the route the homepage gives for the latest code. The homepage gives no runtime, account or hardware requirements.
brief.standout: It is an open implementation of a broadcast and DVD audio codec that most developers never open up. The project name, its origin as an FFmpeg-derived encoder, and its Danish/Norwegian meaning for 'evening' are all unusual touches.
brief.status: Mixed evidence, so I'd call it unknown. The homepage says the current release is Aften 0.0.8 and that 'Development of Aften is very active, and there are some major changes currently in-the-works.' However, the footer reads 'website ©2007 Justin Ruggles', and the page shows no release date for 0.0.8, so the date of the latest activity is unclear.
brief.caveats: The authors state they make no claim that the software or its output is Dolby Digital compliant. Content made with it should not be labelled as containing Dolby Digital technology or carry Dolby trademarks without authorisation. E-AC-3 (Dolby Digital Plus) is not yet supported; it is a future goal. Licensing is mostly LGPL, with some portions under the Xiph.org variant of the BSD licence, and each source file states its own licence. The git clone uses the git:// protocol. The homepage's ©2007 footer and undated release make the maintenance status uncertain.
quotes: Aften is an audio encoder which generates compressed audio streams based on ATSC A/52 specification.
The Aften project started as a stand-alone commandline version of the FFmpeg AC-3 encoder.
E-AC-3 encoding is one of the future goals of the Aften project.
The authors make no claims that this software or any content created with this software is Dolby® Digital compliant.
fetch_log: https://aften.sourceforge.net/ : fetched and loaded. It is a plain website, not a GitHub repository, so no README was returned. The page lists 'Commandline help' and 'Building Aften with CMake' docs, plus a SourceForge project page and a git repository, but gives no URLs for them in the fetched text, so I did not follow them.
